standard.title: Methods for Assessment of Post-Harvest Grain Losses by Rodents — Part 1: General Considerations, Direct Measurement Techniques and Biological Aspects of Survey Procedures; Part 2: Loss Determination by Population Assessment and Estimation Procedures (कृंतकों द्वारा कटाई के बाद अनाज के नुकसान के मूल्यांकन की पद्धतियां — भाग 1: सामान्य विचार, प्रत्यक्ष माप तकनीक और सर्वेक्षण प्रक्रियाओं के जैविक पहलू; भाग 2: जनसंख्या मूल्यांकन और अनुमान प्रक्रियाओं द्वारा नुकसान का निर्धारण)
standard.sector: Food and Agriculture / Post-Harvest Management and Grain Storage

sectional_committee.name: Foodgrains, Allied Products and Ready-to-Eat Foods Sectional Committee

standard.description: This standard specifies scientific guidelines, field survey methodologies, and mathematical estimation procedures for assessing post-harvest grain losses caused by rodents in agricultural warehouses, domestic storage holdings, and processing facilities. Part 1 covers biological traits of primary rodent pests, sign indices, and direct physical measurement techniques. Part 2 details indirect loss determination through rodent population density audits, trap-out removal trapping, and feed-consumption estimation models to guide national crop-preservation and pest-management programs.

certification.description: Voluntary Code of Practice. Since IS 11261 (Parts 1 & 2) is a scientific survey methodology and planning guideline rather than a direct consumer product, it does not carry an individual mandatory BIS 'ISI Mark' product certification stamp. However, compliance with its sampling proformas, trap-out calculations, and biological indicators is highly enforced and mandated in public food storage contracts, warehouse audits (under the Food Corporation of India (FCI), Central Warehousing Corporation (CWC), and state warehousing corporations), and quality evaluations by agricultural ministries to ensure grain security, prevent economic waste, and allocate pest-control resources. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable.
requirements:
Mandates that surveys and loss assessments be planned based on the biological traits, harborage, and breeding habits of the three dominant Indian rodent pests:
a) The Lesser Bandicoot rat (*Bandicota bengalensis*);
b) The House rat (*Rattus rattus*); and
c) The House mouse (*Mus musculus*).

Specifies direct physical techniques to measure grain damage in stored bags, including: collecting representative grain samples, performing sieve analysis to separate and weigh gnawed grain fragments, counting physically damaged bags, and calculating weight discrepancies between initial and terminal storage phases.

Establishes a quantitative, multi-variable formula to calculate total indirect grain losses:
Loss = Rodent Population * Mean Daily Food Consumption * Waste and Contamination Factor * Storage Period.
Notes that rodents contaminate and spoil several times the actual amount of food they consume due to faeces, urine, and hair.

Specifies a multi-night removal trapping (trap-out) method in a designated warehouse sector. Capture rates are plotted over consecutive nights (typically 3 to 5 nights) to mathematically extrapolate the initial absolute rodent population size.

Enforces estimating local rodent populations by introducing measured amounts of non-toxic bait or water and tracking daily consumption before toxic baiting is applied. Total daily consumption is divided by the average daily intake per rodent (e.g., about 10 percent of body weight).

Mandates dividing agricultural survey zones based on crop types and storage types (e.g., traditional mud structures, metal bins, masonry warehouses). Representative sample holdings must be chosen under statistical guidance to conduct direct and indirect audits.

Any observed or calculated survey value, sample size, or percentage grain loss used to determine compliance or report results must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with standard rules per IS 2 : 1960. The number of significant places retained must match the standard's specified value.
